# Native acceptance client images

<!-- Generated by make deps-sync; edit tools/depsync/image-inventory.md.in. -->

Current pins are generated from the acceptance Dockerfiles. The immutable image
and archive digests identify the executable clients. Bundled tools whose exact
versions are not declared in a tag are reported by native CI; a moving image tag
must not inherit an old, manually copied version claim. Passing native CI on the
updated PR commit provides qualification evidence. Historical reports retain their
original tested versions.

## Download sources

The images not listed below take their client from the base image or from the
package manager they run (apk, APT, gem, npm or mix). On an Ubuntu base, APT has
a second mirror too, as the end of this section says. The images below also
download a file while they build. Each file is pinned to the digest its upstream
publishes: a SHA-256, or the SHA-512 that Maven Central and Eclipse publish for
Ivy and Eclipse. Where a second host serves the same bytes, the build falls back
to it, so one host being down does not fail the build
([#1321](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1321),
[#1322](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1322)).
[`fetch-pinned.sh`](../../test/acceptance/clients/fetch-pinned.sh) tries each
source in turn and keeps the first file whose digest matches the pin. It passes
over a source that answers with other bytes as it does one that does not answer,
so a second source never changes what runs. When every source is down, the build
fails. A pin names the first URL only; `make deps-sync` moves the second URL with
it. A source can also be the first URL through a named host (`URL via HOST`),
for a download host whose name a traffic manager hands to more than one
delivery network; curl connects to HOST and still checks the URL's own host
name. The `tools/depsync` tests fail when an image that downloads a file has no
row below, or names a second source here but fetches without `fetch-pinned.sh`
or the pip loop.

The Python images, listed below too, install their clients and every
dependency with pip from a hashed requirements file
([#1439](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1439)).
[`pip-lock.sh`](../../test/acceptance/clients/pip-lock.sh) writes each `.txt`
file from the pins in its `.in` file, with PyPI's SHA-256 for every file of each
pinned release. pip installs the whole file with `--require-hashes`, from PyPI
and then from the second index, so the second index can serve only PyPI's bytes.
It builds no sdist (`--only-binary=:all:`), except PyYAML in the Ansible image,
whose build requirements are hashed in a file of their own
(`--build-constraint`). To move a pin, edit the `.in` file and run
`pip-lock.sh`; the `tools/depsync` tests fail while a `.txt` file lags its `.in`
file. The CI-installed Hugging Face and Conan clients work the same way. Conan
1.66.0 and two of its dependencies publish only sdists, and the pip of the
job's Python 3.12 venv has no `--build-constraint`, so the Conan step installs
the setuptools that builds them from a hashed file of its own first and builds
them with `--no-build-isolation`
([#1455](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1455)).

The images that install packages with APT on an Ubuntu base (Git LFS, JetBrains,
opkg, P2, Vagrant and VS Code on 26.10, Swift on 22.04) give each Canonical host
in the base image's sources a second mirror
([#1632](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1632)). Before
the first `apt-get update` they run
[`ubuntu-mirrors.sh`](../../test/acceptance/clients/ubuntu-mirrors.sh), which
turns each such source, in 26.10's deb822 `ubuntu.sources` or 22.04's one-line
`sources.list`, into a `mirror+file:` list of that host and then its second
mirror, each with a priority, since APT otherwise tries a list's mirrors in
random order. APT retries a file on the host three times, its default since APT
2.3.2, and then fetches it from the second mirror. APT before 3.1.3, which
22.04 ships, can wait for good on a file it queued again after a delay
([LP: #2003851](https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/apt/+bug/2003851),
open for 22.04), and the Swift image's `apt-get update` hung that way with
`archive.ubuntu.com` refused. So on such an APT the script sets
`Acquire::Retries` to 0, and a file goes to the second mirror at its first
failure. A second mirror can serve
only what Canonical signed: APT checks each suite's `InRelease` against the
Ubuntu archive key in the base image, and every index and package against the
SHA-256 in that signed file, whichever mirror serves it, and nothing turns that
check off. When every mirror is down, the build fails. The script fails the build
when the base image's sources name none of the hosts below, or one it did not
rewrite, and the `tools/depsync` tests fail when an image runs `apt-get` without
it, other than the Debian images, whose `deb.debian.org` is Debian's own CDN.
The Debian client image installs nothing; it reports the APT of its base image.

| Source in the base image | Second mirror |
|---|---|
| `archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu`, for the release and its `-updates` and `-backports` | `azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu`, the Ubuntu mirror inside Azure. GitHub's own Ubuntu runner images install from it, with `archive.ubuntu.com` as their failover ([`configure-apt-sources.sh`](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/main/images/ubuntu/scripts/build/configure-apt-sources.sh)), and it is on Microsoft's network, apart from the Canonical hosts the runners could not reach on 2026-11-16. It served the same `InRelease` as `archive.ubuntu.com` for every suite when #1632 checked |
| `security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu`, for `-security` | `azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu`, which carries `-security` too |
| `ports.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-ports`, for every suite of an arm64 build | `mirrors.ocf.berkeley.edu/ubuntu-ports`, UC Berkeley's Open Computing Facility, a ports mirror on [Launchpad's list](https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+archivemirrors). `azure.ports.ubuntu.com` resolves to `ports.ubuntu.com`'s own hosts, so it is no second source. It can lag `ports.ubuntu.com` by some hours, so an arm64 build that falls back to it can install the update before the latest, still one Canonical signed. CI builds only amd64 |

The Puppet image stays on Ruby 3.3 through a Dependabot entry of its own,
because the pinned Puppet cannot extract a module archive on Ruby 3.4
([#1126](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1126)). The
npm 12 image stays on Node 24 LTS the same way: it keeps the prior Node line
beside the newest Node ([decision 0034](../research/decisions/0034-npm.md)).
The `dotnet-10` image stays on the .NET SDK's 10.0 LTS line the same way,
beside the newest line in `dotnet.Dockerfile`
([#1229](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1229)).

The Hex image is the one that Dependabot does not move. `hexpm/elixir` holds a
tag for every combination of Elixir, Erlang/OTP and OS release, about a million,
and Docker Hub answers 504 when Dependabot lists them, even 100 at a time
([#1240](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1240)). So
Dependabot ignores the image, and `deps-refresh.yml` moves it with
`tools/depsync/hex_image.py`. The script takes the newest Elixir release and the
newest OTP and Alpine image that `hexpm/elixir` publishes for it, through Docker
Hub's name-filtered tag API. It pins the tag by digest and never moves a part of
the pin backwards. The move goes up on `deps/hex-image` and needs the same review
as any client image. The official `elixir` image has few tags, but they name only
the OTP major, so the declared pins could no longer name the exact OTP release.
Dependabot also misorders those tags: from `1.20.5-otp-29-alpine` it would
propose `1.20-otp-28-alpine`.

Every base is a stable release. `tools/depsync/sync.py` refuses an acceptance
Dockerfile whose `FROM` tag carries a prerelease marker after its version, such
as `-118.1.beta`, `a1`, `rc1`, `-dev` or `-preview`, and names the file, the tag
and the marker. Variant suffixes such as `-slim`, `-alpine` or `-bookworm` pass.
Dependabot proposes such tags for `python` and `dart`, whose `latest` tag shares
its digest with no full version tag, so `.github/dependabot.yml` ignores their
prereleases by version range
([#1223](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1223),
[#1304](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/1304)).

Purposeful compatibility lanes retain their declared runtimes. Updating a pin
regenerates this inventory, recipe labels and secondary version assertions; it
does not bypass native tests or the review required for acceptance client changes.
[QUAL-01 #792](https://github.com/weaveplatform/artifactweave/issues/792) records
the final merged-main qualification. See [dependency maintenance](dependency-maintenance.md).
